maria: Kicking off phase 2 of runtime ownership demarcation. Goal is to make explicit who is responsible for short‑path request routing, eviction decisions, and policy enforcement across hosted / dedicated / private deployments.
ben: 👍 can you list the hard constraints we need to honor? latency SLO, cost, security, etc.
alisa: Quick Q — do we want eviction decision logic centralized in the control plane or kept local in the runtime?
carlos: My vote is local-first. Runtime handles fast decisions (LRU / token-based) to avoid P95 regressions. Control plane should supply policy and audit, not be in the hot path.
vicky: Agreed on local-first. We should define a small runtime API for eviction probes + forced evict and an event stream back to control plane. Policy expressed as a compact JSON manifest so private installs can seed it locally.
ben: Can we define a minimal policy manifest? Rough example: 
```json
{
  "policy_version": "v2",
  "evict_threshold_ms": 120,
  "priority_buckets": ["reserved", "on_demand"],
  "secret_handling": "no_secrets_in_shared_runtime"
}
```
devops-bot: heads up: implementing forced-evict endpoint will spike eviction traffic during load-tests — update CI load scenarios.
alisa: Another edge: private / air-gapped customers may never reach control plane. Runtime must have durable local policy store + clear default fallbacks so it is safe standalone.
sam: For testing, propose a mixed-workload harness: 70% hosted, 20% dedicated, 10% private traffic with eviction churn. Measure P95, tail OOMs, and unit-cost delta.
maria: Also require decision trace: who/what caused eviction. Add a decision_id and decision_reason in events so audits can reconstruct flows.
vicky: :thumbsup: I'll draft the RFC for manifest schema + runtime endpoints. Timeline: 1 week RFC, 2 week prototype.
ben: Rollout plan idea — canary in hosted staging, then opt-in for dedicated customers, then customer-by-customer for private. Document migration steps.
carlos: Fallback semantics note: if runtime cannot evict due to lack of permissions or resource constraints, it should attempt local emergency heuristics first. Calling control plane is secondary and only if reachable and allowed by deployment mode.
alisa: Summarizing the rule: runtime-first local decisions; control plane for policy config, telemetry, and optional remote overrides (but never required for correctness in private installs).
maria: Action items: vicky -> write manifest + RFC; sam -> test harness scenarios; carlos -> runtime endpoints (/evict_probe, /evict_force) spec; alisa -> control plane policy API and sync semantics. I'll record the decision in the architecture tracker.
vicky: Will share a draft doc and a link to the prototype branch once available.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: evict-proto branch -> staging (CI will run checks).
ben: Thanks all — keeping thread here for follow-ups and questions.
